title: Past Simple: Regular Verbs (-ed)

Distinguish the three pronunciations of -ed: /t/, /d/, and /ɪd/

sections.title: Spelling Rules for Regular Past Simple
sections.content:
The **Past Simple** expresses actions that started and finished at a specific time in the past.

For regular verbs, we add **-ed** to the base form of the verb for all subjects (I, you, he, she, it, we, they).

However, watch out for these four spelling rules:

tables.title: Regular Verb -ed Spelling Rules
rows: Consonant + vowel + consonant (CVC): double last letter

callouts.title: The /ɪd/ Rule
callouts.text: Only pronounce -ed as an extra syllable (/ɪd/) when the base verb ends in a **T** or **D** sound! For all other verbs, -ed does not add an extra syllable.

callouts.title: Negative Statements
callouts.text: In negative sentences, use **did not (didn't) + base verb**: 'I didn't walk' (NOT 'I didn't walked').

timeline.title: Completed Action in the Past
timeline.past: Yesterday at 3 PM: I cleaned the kitchen (Action finished)
timeline.explanation: Past simple verbs indicate completed events whose time is finished.

exercises.prompt: Which of the following regular verbs requires doubling the final consonant before -ed?
exercises.explanation: 'stop' is a single-syllable verb ending in a single consonant preceded by a single vowel (CVC: t-o-p), so the final 'p' doubles: 'stopped'.
exercises.urduExplanation: 'stop' ایک حرفی لفظ ہے جس میں ایک ہی vowel کے بعد ایک consonant ہے، اس لیے آخری حرف دوگنا ہو جاتا ہے: stopped۔

exercises.prompt: Find and correct the error in this sentence: 'They didn't wanted to leave the party early.'
exercises.correctAnswer: They didn't want to leave the party early.
acceptableAnswers: They didn't want to leave the party early.
They did not want to leave the party early.
exercises.explanation: After the auxiliary 'did not' or 'didn't', the main verb must remain in its base form ('want', not 'wanted').
exercises.urduExplanation: جب جملے میں 'didn't' آ جائے تو اس کے بعد اصل فعل ہمیشہ پہلی فارم (base form) میں رہتا ہے۔

exercises.prompt: The verb 'decided' ends with the /_____/ sound because its base form ends in a 'd' sound.
exercises.explanation: Verbs ending with the /t/ or /d/ sound take the extra-syllable pronunciation /ɪd/: de-ci-ded.
exercises.urduExplanation: جن افعال کا اختتام t یا d کی آواز پر ہوتا ہے، ان کا -ed 'ɪd' کے طور پر بولا جاتا ہے۔

exercises.prompt: Listen and repeat with clear pronunciation: 'I worked all morning and walked home in the evening.'
exercises.audioPrompt: I worked all morning and walked home in the evening.
exercises.explanation: Notice the voiceless /t/ sound at the end of both 'worked' (/wɜːrkt/) and 'walked' (/wɔːkt/).
exercises.urduExplanation: worked اور walked کے آخر میں 't' کی آواز صاف طور پر ادا کریں۔

sections.title: ماضی قریب کے بارے میں اردو نوٹس
sections.urduText: اردو میں ہم کہتے ہیں: 'میں نے کام کیا'، 'وہ چلے گئے'۔ انگریزی میں باقاعدہ افعال (Regular Verbs) کے ساتھ صرف -ed کا اضافہ کیا جاتا ہے۔ منفی جملوں کے لیے 'didn't' کا استعمال ہوتا ہے، اور یاد رہے کہ 'didn't' کے بعد فعل کی پہلی شکل (First Form) ہی آئے گی، مثلاً: 'I didn't work' (نہ کہ 'I didn't worked')۔

sections.title: Key Takeaways
summaryPoints: Regular verbs take -ed in the past simple for all subjects.
Doubling rule applies to single-syllable CVC verbs (stop -> stopped, plan -> planned).
Only add an extra syllable /ɪd/ if the base verb ends in /t/ or /d/ (waited, decided).
